reasoning: Both attempts keep server code off clients, mark the client module ClientOnly, ship the remote as a child instance, validate requests fully and notify through NotificationServerService only when the spot is too far. A wins because it follows the NotificationSystem split properly: the catalog and baseplate registration and the notification mediator are in Implementation. B leaves Implementation empty. B's client module is also copied to clients and uses relative requires into Modules/Catalogs and Utilities, which could fail there; A uses absolute @game paths that work on both realms. The luau-lsp failures in both are path-lookup errors in the checker, not code errors.

criteria.note: Gameplay/BlockPlacementSystem has SystemPackage (services, BlockPlacementNetwork with a PlaceBlock child) and Implementation (_BlockPlacementSetup and _BlockPlacementNotificationMediator, which hold the game wiring); no new scripts.

criteria.criterion: Server code stays on the server
criteria.note: BlockPlacementServerService.meta.json and _BlockPlacementNotificationMediator.meta.json both set RelocateToServerScriptService: true.

criteria.criterion: Client code runs only on clients

criteria.note: The remote is a child of the module (script:WaitForChild on its own child), and the Baseplate wait runs inside task.spawn in _BlockPlacementSetup:Init.
Modules copied to clients use @game absolute paths for BlockTypes and Grid; the server-only mediator requires NotificationServerService; there is no second remote.

tryPlaceBlock checks the rate limit, string type, catalog lookup, Vector3 and NaN, the floor height, 64-stud reach and filled cells; only TooFar notifies. Keys One to Five follow the registered list, and both MouseButton1 and TouchTap place.
Strict mode and typed rejection reasons, with no edits to existing files. The setmetatable inheritance from the shared service is a little indirect.
Building/PlacementSystem's Implementation folder contains only an init.meta.json; the game-specific wiring (BlockTypes catalog, Baseplate lookup) sits inside the SystemPackage services.

criteria.criterion: Server code stays on the server
criteria.note: PlacementServerService.meta.json and PlacementRules.meta.json both set RelocateToServerScriptService: true.

criteria.criterion: Client code runs only on clients

criteria.note: The remote is a child of PlacementNetwork; Init uses FindFirstChild plus assert and never yields.

The client service, which is copied to clients, requires ../../../../Catalogs/BlockTypes and ../../../../Utilities/Grid by relative path, which only works if those folders are also copied to ReplicatedStorage. The notification correctly goes through NotificationServerService.

onPlaceBlockRequested checks the rate limit, the catalog via ByName, isSanePosition (Vector3, finite, inside bounds), isAboveFloor, isWithinReach (where notifyTooFar is called) and filled cells. Keys follow BlockTypes.List, and the client handles mouse clicks plus touch taps (short, small-movement touches).
Readable code with typed rules, but no --!strict. The extra world-bounds rule was not asked for, though it is reasonable.

strengths: Clean SystemPackage/Implementation split, with the catalog and the notification wired in Implementation
Absolute @game requires work on both realms
A complete validation chain with only the too-far case notified, plus a notification cooldown
weaknesses: The shared service's setmetatable inheritance adds indirection
The setup module runs on both realms and depends on Init order only loosely

strengths: Pure PlacementRules module, covered by a spec
Robust tap detection that ignores camera drags
Uses the hit block's center to find the neighboring cell
weaknesses: Empty Implementation folder; the game wiring lives in SystemPackage
Relative requires from a client-copied module to Catalogs and Utilities could fail on the client
